comparison: Perfect agreement on AlphaFold2 structural predictions (C2-C4, C19-C27). Both evaluations find the structural models, buried surface area calculations, and 1:1:2 stoichiometry well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the clarity and quality of structural data.

Complete agreement on ATG13-ULK1 interaction validation (C29-C32). Both evaluations confirm that structural predictions are validated by ITC, point mutations, and cellular assays. Peer reviewers explicitly note the biochemical confirmation and identification of critical residues.

Strong agreement on ATG13-FIP200 interaction and MIT-MIM contacts (C33-C38, C44). OpenEval focuses on structural similarity to yeast and validation by ITC/mutations. Peer review (R3) combines this with ULK1 stabilization claims (C39-C43), confirming biochemical validation and high data quality across all ATG13 interactions.

OpenEval addresses ULK1 stabilization by ATG13 (C39-C43) as a separate result. Peer review R3 groups this with broader ATG13 interaction validation, confirming the extensive binary interactions. Both find the evidence convincing, though organized differently.

Perfect agreement on direct ULK1-FIP200 interaction (C45-C52). Both evaluations accept the AlphaFold2 predictions, pull-down assays, and cellular co-IP data. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the extensive binary interactions and note no concerns about this finding.

Both address functional consequences of disrupting interactions (C53-C56), but peer review R5 combines this with broader functional data (C5-C6, C57-C64, C80). OpenEval finds partial phenotype well-explained by redundancy. Peer reviewers praise the CRISPR KI approach and find functional data convincing.

Strong agreement on additive effects of mutations and complementary interactions (C57-C64, C80). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent effects and FLAG-tag controls (C61-C62). Peer review highlights this as a strength, noting the CRISPR KI approach demonstrates partial redundancy of ATG13-ULK1 and ATG13-FIP200 interactions.

Agreement on colocalization observation (C65-C66), but both express caution. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation about p62 body recruitment is speculative. Peer review implicitly accepts through lack of challenge, but this finding is supplementary and not extensively discussed.

Both address ATG14 Ser29 phosphorylation (C68-C69). OpenEval finds the mechanistic link supported but notes unexplained complexity. Peer review R6 indicates initial concerns about ULK1 kinase activity were addressed in revision, suggesting acceptance of phosphorylation data. OpenEval also addresses C67 not covered by peer review.

Perfect agreement on structural comparison with yeast (C70-C73). Both evaluations accept the structural differences and functional consequences regarding bridging and higher-order assemblage. Peer reviewers note the work builds consensus for ULK1 complex structure compared to yeast.

Complete agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation of physiological significance claims (C74-C79, C81). Both note that while splicing variants exist (documented in literature), the proposed tissue-specific regulation is speculative without experimental validation. Neither evaluation challenges the facts but both question interpretations.

OpenEval addresses summary claims C5-C6 separately, finding them well-supported by collective evidence. Peer review R5 integrates these claims with functional data (C53-C64, C80), praising the overall demonstration that ATG13's dual interactions are essential for full autophagy response.

Partial overlap on FLAG-tag control observations (C61-C62). OpenEval includes these as technical controls in functional analysis. Peer review R10 implicitly accepts these technical limitations, with Reviewer 3 praising the CRISPR KI approach while acknowledging its constraints.

OpenEval separately evaluates background/context claims (C1, C7-C18, C28) as supported by literature citations. Peer review does not separately address these established knowledge claims, focusing instead on novel findings.
